newsitem.title: UK: Dollar weighed lower at European close after data.
newsitem.headline: Dollar weighed lower at European close after data.

text.p: The dollar closed softer here after a set of weaker than expected U.S. economic data dampened prospects for a near-term rise in interest rates, traders said.
The employment cost index, a key indicator for the Federal Reserve to gauge wage inflation, rose 0.6 percent in the first quarter, less than the 0.9 percent rise expected by economists.
Durable goods data, down 3.0 percent in March on the month, and a softer than expected April consumer confidence index at 116.8 percent, also weighed on the dollar.
"The data dented rate rise hopes, and that's pulling the dollar lower," said David Bloom at HSBC James Capel.
At 1615 GMT the dollar was at 1.7230/40 marks, down from 1.7265/75 in late Europe on Monday. Against the yen, it was at 126.68/78, little changed from 126.58/63.
Dealers said the fall below support at 1.7260 was bearish for the dollar short-term and further slippage to 1.72 marks likely.
But expectations of firm first-quarter GDP figures, due on Wednesday and strong non-farm payrolls on Friday, should help keep the dollar well supported, traders said.
"The market is rather thin at the moment, but we should continue to see the dollar well supported on dips," said Chris Furness, currency strategist at 4Cast.

A strong non-farm payroll figure would invigorate rate rise speculation. Bloom at HSBC James Capel expects a 160,000 rise in non-farm payrolls in April, below the consensus forecast for an increase of 211,000.
"The dollar remains well supported by fundamentals, and until the picture of a robust U.S. economy remains intact, it's going to be well underpinned," said Bloom, a currency economist.

Analysts were doubtful whether the data would be enough to stop the Federal Reserve from tightening again at its next meeting in May. The Federal funds target rate was raised by 25 basis points to 5.5 percent on March 25.
Buoyant U.S. asset markets provided a prop for the dollar, traders said. The Dow Jones was up 100 points in morning trading and Treasury bonds were up 1-1/2 points after the data.

Elsewhere, sterling gained against the softer dollar and also held firm against the mark. With only two days ahead of the election, the pound is fairly rangebound as opinion polls continue to show a clear lead of the opposition Labour party.
Sterling/mark was at 2.8110/20 from 2.8040/50 at the previous European close, while cable rose to $1.6300/10 from $1.6234/44.
The French franc was unsettled by a new opinion poll, giving the centre-right coalition just 39 percent of the vote.
Mark/French franc was at 3.3729/33 against 3.3716/19 in late Europe on Monday.
